coaching.headline: Lost on structures, one taken to ten lost: three won fights bought no towers, and the jungle bled eleven deaths, the game's most.

flags.text: After a 2-0 offlane win, Gadget and Sparrow razed two allied inhibitors and an inner inside a minute.
Boris died eleven damn times, more than double the norm: four to Serath, four outside any detected fight.
Allied Mini Prime cost three deaths, Boris at the Prime pit first, and no enemy structure fell afterward.
Skylar was the damn bright spot: nine kills topped the lobby, three on Sparrow.

focus.title: Wins go to towers, the jungler goes with company
focus.action: After any won fight, all five group on the nearest enemy tower or the allied structure under siege, and Boris contests Fangtooth or Prime only beside at least two allies.

21.call: Lost 0-3 on the duo lane and in the allied jungle half a minute after Boris and Riktor fell; Fangtooth and the allied mid outer then went enemy. Jungler dead, concede Fangtooth and hold mid.

32.5.call: Lost 3-5 after Orb Prime and Primal Fangtooth went enemy; Boris died first to Gadget, then the mid inhibitor and Core fell. Facing both buffs, hold the base as five.

24.8.call: Lost 1-3 on the duo lane: Sparrow killed Argus, Countess and Boris and destroyed the allied duo outer during the fight. When Argus falls first, give up the outer and regroup.

cdbec113-f2c2-43d9-b3ea-c811fade30df: Took the only enemy structure the team got, the offlane outer. Next time an outer falls, call the jungler over and push the inner before backing.
Five deaths on a norm under three, two to Riktor and one to The Fey outside any detected fight. When both are unseen, rotate beside a teammate.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: Farm was strong at 10.4 CS per minute on a 7.3 norm, plus three kills on Serath. Before any rotation, shove the mid wave first.
Three deaths to Sparrow, two on duo-lane rotations, and the allied mid outer fell after the first. When Sparrow shows on the duo lane, rotate there only beside Skylar.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Objective damage was 331, the lowest of all ten players, against Sparrow's 19245. When the team starts Fangtooth or Prime, hit the monster before chasing kills.
Two duo-lane deaths before minute eight, one to Serath outside any detected fight shortly before the first enemy Fangtooth. Until Serath shows elsewhere, farm behind the wave.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Kill participation hit 50% with 39% of team assists and zero deaths before minute ten. When Serath goes missing early, ward the duo-lane river.
Nine wards beat a norm of six, but Gadget placed 19 and the enemy out-cleared the team nine to two. Before each Fangtooth, have three wards up near the pit.
2595aadd-bde2-44ec-a166-0e4b63c357d0: Died at a pit three times within seconds of an enemy take: Mini Prime once, Fangtooth twice. When the enemy starts Fangtooth, trade for Mini Prime instead.
10885 gold against Serath's 15978, on 5.8 CS per minute versus a 7.5 norm. Until the gold gap closes, clear allied camps and skip Serath's jungle.

matchup: Riktor was the lane opponent and killed Greystone twice; Greystone killed Riktor once, in the allied jungle.
Riktor chains Riplash pull, Shock Therapy silence and Skewer suppress; silences and suppressions also halt the target's cooldowns.
Basic-attacking Riktor triggers Tainted Guard: 45% less healing for 3s, so open trades with abilities.
build: Augmentation is the one winning-core item built; Overlord and Tainted Blade from the 54.6% core never made the build.
Unbroken Will's Undying raises both armors 25% for 2.5s whenever Greystone is immobilized, useful into Riktor, Gadget and The Fey.
Legacy, the last item finished, cleanses and grants 3s of crowd-control immunity below 40% health, once per 60s.
eternal: Idrisil adds 15% to both armors above 30% health; dropping below spends that bonus on an armor-scaled shield.
Krix and Xyris are a toss-up for the Greystone offlane lead, Krix with the best odds; Idrisil trails both.
Cold Hearted with Icy Touch is the best Idrisil pair; Mending with Diamond Tip has too few games to rank.
augment: Tainted Oath makes Sacred Oath apply 50% Blight to enemies for 4.5s.
Imperial Soul is clearly the field's best Greystone offlane augment; Tainted Oath ranks third.
crest: Atlas, the Saphir's Mantle active, grows size and max health 10% for 6s, then keeps 20% of damage dealt as max health.
Iceskorn Talons and Brutallax are a toss-up for the lead; Saphir's Mantle ranks fourth among crests with enough games.
Iceskorn Talons and Brutallax evolve from Champion Crest; Saphir's Mantle from Goliath Crest.
improvement: Imperial Soul over Tainted Oath is the field-backed swap: a larger, harder-hitting Stone Forged Soul, giving up the Blight.
Iceskorn Talons over Saphir's Mantle trades permanent health for an ice sheet granting allies physical power and speed.

matchup: The Fey was the lane opponent: 7/2/15 with 47525 hero damage, the game's most, and Countess never killed The Fey.
Fly Trap attaches to nearby heroes, pulls inward and stuns; spread before committing Feast so one pull cannot catch two.
build: Combustion, Noxia and Wraith Leggings are the full 49% winning core.
Noxia's Dark Matter adds 6% max-health damage when a second ability hits a hero the first one marked.
Overseer makes Feast deal 15% more damage and heal 25% of the damage dealt to heroes.
eternal: Vesh repeats 7% of ability damage on heroes as damage over 3s, growing each minute.
Lotus leans ahead in the Countess midlane field; Vesh ranks third of three Eternals with enough games.
Lich with Mind Rot is the best Vesh pair. Sound keep on minors.
augment: Sanguine Slash: Blade Siphon deals 20% more damage and heals 50% more against isolated targets.
Shadow Echo and Sanguine Slash are a toss-up in the Countess midlane field; Shadow Echo has the best odds. Sound keep.
crest: Anima, the Soulbearer active, gives an 8s shield plus 20% magical lifesteal and 10% movement speed.
Tempest, Voidgazer and Epoch are a toss-up for the lead; Soulbearer ranks fourth among crests with enough games.
Voidgazer, Epoch and Soulbearer evolve from Wizard Crest; Tempest from Warlock Crest.
improvement: Lotus over Vesh is the field-backed Eternal test: random stat gains every takedown and two minutes, giving up the damage echo.
Tempest over Soulbearer trades the shield for damage to three nearby heroes each second, healing 35% of that damage.

matchup: Duo was Skylar and Argus against Sparrow and Gadget; Skylar killed Sparrow three times and Argus killed Gadget twice.
Sparrow's Relentless stacks add max-health damage on hit; short trades deny the stacking.
The Fey killed Skylar twice; Skylar killed Serath three times and The Fey twice.
build: Plasma Blade, Vanquisher and Imperator are the full 50.1% winning core; Demolisher is the extra.
Demolisher ignores 25% of physical armor, and basic attacks and critical strikes also ignore 30% of bonus physical armor.
Vanquisher's Annihilate executes heroes brought under 5% health.
eternal: Weald fires true-damage missiles after damaging a hero below 30% health, with a 10s cooldown per hero.
Thraex, Xyris and Weald are a toss-up in the Skylar carry field; Thraex has the best odds. Sound keep.
The Forage and Wind-Rider minors are the top Weald pair.
augment: Assault MK-II extends the Air Assault hover by 0.5s and adds a missile to each attack.
Assault MK-II leans ahead in the Skylar carry field. Sound keep.
crest: Pacifier's Adrenalize dashes, empowers the next physical hit, and can be recast after a hero kill within 3s.
Eviscerator leans ahead of Pacifier in the Skylar carry field.
Eviscerator and Pacifier both evolve from Sharpshooter Crest.
improvement: Eviscerator over Pacifier is the field-backed swap: 6s of attack speed and omnivamp, giving up the dash and recast.
On Eternal, minors and augment, no change is proven.

matchup: Serath killed Argus twice, in the allied jungle and base; Sparrow once, as the first death of the duo-lane teamfight.
Gadget's Security Gate roots and Tesla Dome shreds magical armor each tick; Spellbreaker's Veil blocks the next ability.
build: Timewarp, Dynamo and Tainted Scepter are the full 49.2% winning core; Spellbreaker is the extra.
Dynamo: a hero Argus immobilizes, as with the Dread Nova stun, takes 8% more damage for 2.5s.
Tainted Scepter was the last item finished, so the full Tainted Scepter healing cut on healers Gadget and Riktor came late.
eternal: Vesh echoes a share of ability damage as damage over 3s; Mind Rot adds 2% of current health.
Vesh and Lotus are a toss-up in the Argus support field; Vesh has the best odds. Sound keep.
Lich with Mind Rot is the best Vesh pair; Tithe of Death with Mind Rot is the most played.
augment: Infinite Obliteration gives Synaptic Obliterator infinite-range beams that travel 50% faster and slow 50% longer.
Arcane Engine leans ahead in the Argus support field; Infinite Obliteration ranks second.
crest: Silentium's Muzzle silences a hero for 0.75s, and Visionary raises the ward cap to three.
Leafsong and Tranquility are a toss-up for the lead; Silentium ranks last of six crests with enough games.
Leafsong evolves from Warden Crest; Tranquility and Silentium from Keeper Crest.
improvement: Lich over Tithe of Death is the field-backed minor swap: magical lifesteal instead of takedown mana and haste.
Arcane Engine over Infinite Obliteration trades beam range for stacking movement speed on ability hits.
Tranquility over Silentium keeps the three-ward cap and swaps the silence for a group heal.

matchup: Serath was the jungle opponent and killed Boris four times, including first blood; Boris never killed Serath.
Heaven's Fury makes Serath crowd-control immune and invulnerable during the dash; hold Ursine Burst until Serath reappears.
build: Basilisk is the one winning-core item; Sky Splitter and Rapture from the 50.4% core never made the build.
Syonic Echo gives the next three basic attacks 30% attack speed after each cast and, on melee heroes, resets the basic attack.
Aegis of Agawar adds 10% to both armors, rising to 20% below 40% health.
eternal: Marrow turns hero damage into healing, more at low health; Roses pays only on takedowns, and Boris had four.
Weald and Exarch are a toss-up for the Boris jungle lead, Weald with the best odds; Marrow ranks last of four.
Blood Bank with The Maw is the best Marrow pair; Blood Bank with Roses is the most played.
augment: Bolster Bearicade raises both armors 15% while Tesseract Core is active, which needs max Canisters.
Apex Hunter and Savage Shred are a toss-up for the lead; Bolster Bearicade ranks third of three.
crest: Glacial Colosseum, the Iceskorn Talons active, lays an 8s ice sheet: allies gain physical power and speed, enemies slow 10%.
Liberator leans ahead in the Boris jungle field; Iceskorn Talons ranks fifth of seven crests with enough games.
Liberator evolves from Sharpshooter Crest; Iceskorn Talons from Champion Crest.
improvement: Weald over Marrow is the field-backed Eternal swap: true-damage missiles on low-health heroes, giving up the healing.
Apex Hunter over Bolster Bearicade adds 70% Chrono Swipe damage to heroes under 20% max health, giving up the armor.
Liberator over Iceskorn Talons trades the ice sheet for a full cleanse and a shield.

threats: Chain-CC risk (4 hard-CC abilities, ~3.5s of lockdown): Gadget Security Gate (root 1s), Riktor Riplash (pull), Riktor Shock Therapy (silence 0.8s), Riktor Skewer (suppress 1.25s). Don't group tight into it — stagger the engage and hold mobility/cleanse for the key one.
Heal-stacking: Gadget, Riktor. Anti-heal is mandatory against this comp — we brought 2 items of it.
Dive threat on our backline: Serath. Assign peel for the carry and ward the flanks.
synergy: Our engage/CC: Countess Feast (suppress 0.75s). Our kills come from landing burst INSIDE that CC window — whoever lands it, the rest must follow up immediately.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.

ourKits.combo: Assault The Gates leap → Make Way armor shred → Sacred Oath empowered basic → Stone Forged Soul stasis ult
ourKits.winCondition: front-line aggressively and reset the fight with the stasis heal
ourKits.playWith: a team that fights while he soaks and stasis-resets
ourKits.playAgainst: don't waste burst into his stasis — wait it out; anti-heal cuts the ult heal

ourKits.combo: Shadow Slip in → Eventide → Blade Siphon → Feast suppress ult, Haemorrhage true-damage
ourKits.winCondition: Feast-suppress a squishy and delete them with true-damage burst
ourKits.passive: two-ability hits apply a %max-HP true-damage bleed
ourKits.playWith: a team to clean up after her pick
ourKits.playAgainst: Feast is her whole engage — bait it / peel; she's fragile, punish the recast window

ourKits.combo: Plasma Grenade → Hypercharge on-hit → Air Assault reposition → Atomiser ult
ourKits.winCondition: Hypercharge and kite-shoot from Air Assault safety
ourKits.passive: extra jump; kills cause corpse explosions
ourKits.playWith: a frontline so she can free-fire airborne
ourKits.playAgainst: CC her out of Air Assault; she's squishy on the ground

ourKits.combo: Dread Nova stun → Ether Crystal push/lift → Particle Shredder channel → Synaptic Obliterator beams
ourKits.winCondition: poke from max range and zone with the crystal
ourKits.playWith: a frontline to protect his stationary channel
ourKits.playAgainst: dodge Dread Nova; dive him during the immobile ult channel

ourKits.combo: Detection Protocol track → Chrono Swipe → Primeval Roar shield → Ursine Burst grab ult
ourKits.winCondition: grab a key target out of position and burst them down
ourKits.playWith: a team that collapses on his grabbed target
ourKits.playAgainst: his grab ult is the whole threat — bait it / stay spaced; CC during Primeval Roar

enemyKits.combo: Ascend dive → Heaven's Fury multi-strike → Chastise slow → Heresy form ult, resets on takedowns
enemyKits.winCondition: dive the backline and snowball Heresy resets
enemyKits.playWith: a frontline that creates her dive angle
enemyKits.playAgainst: peel the backline — deny the first kill and her resets dry up

enemyKits.combo: Security Gate root → Sticky Mine → Tesla Dome zone ult
enemyKits.winCondition: root with the gate and trap a fight inside the Tesla Dome
enemyKits.passive: FDA stacks grant scaling magical power
enemyKits.playWith: frontline that holds enemies in her Dome
enemyKits.playAgainst: dodge the gate; spread vs the Dome — she's immobile, dive her

enemyKits.combo: Piercing Shot poke → Heightened Senses AS → Hail of Arrows zone → Inner Fire ult
enemyKits.winCondition: ramp Relentless + AS and sustained-DPS the front down
enemyKits.playWith: heavy peel — she's immobile and pure DPS
enemyKits.playAgainst: she has zero escape — hard-engage her and she dies first

enemyKits.combo: Riplash pull → Shock Therapy silence → Skewer suppress ult
enemyKits.winCondition: pull a target in and chain silence+suppress for a guaranteed kill
enemyKits.playWith: burst that deletes his pulled/suppressed target
enemyKits.playAgainst: respect Riplash range — stay spaced; cleanse/QSS the suppress

enemyKits.combo: Bramble Patch slow → Harvest Nettles stacks → Untamed Growth DoT → Fly Trap pull ult
enemyKits.winCondition: Fly Trap a clumped team and detonate AoE on the pull
enemyKits.passive: takedowns spawn growths + grant move speed
enemyKits.playWith: engage that clumps for her Fly Trap
enemyKits.playAgainst: spread out vs the pull; she's squishy — dive her

checks.text: No real tank: nobody to start fights or take the first hits for the backline.
Out-tanked 0 v 1: teams one tank down won 47% in 1.18.
3 divers (Greystone, Boris, Countess): each one past the first is a hero not holding the line.
One main mage and one main marksman at most.
Argus at support is a mage: nobody stays with the carry.

teamComp.summary: Draft: 0 tanks, 3 divers vs their 1 tank, 1 diver. In 1.18 ranked, our shape won 48% and theirs 50.9%.
